# 92 Hepatic Metastasis from Noncolorectal Nonneuroendocrine Tumors

1. **What percentage of malignant liver tumors are primary liver or bile duct cancers?**  
    A. 5%  
    B. 15%  
    C. 25%  
    **D. 10%**  
    *Correct: D. Only 10% of malignant liver tumors are primary liver or bile duct cancers, with the vast majority being metastatic lesions.*

2. **What is the 5-year overall survival rate for patients with resected noncolorectal nonneuroendocrine (NCNN) liver metastases according to large studies?**  
    A. 25-30%  
    B. 50-55%  
    C. 15-20%  
    **D. 36-41%**  
    *Correct: D. Large studies report 5-year overall survival rates of 36-41% for patients with resected NCNN liver metastases.*

3. **Which primary tumor type with liver metastases has the best prognosis after hepatic resection according to Sano et al.?**  
    A. Pancreatic cancer  
    B. Breast cancer  
    C. Ovarian cancer  
    **D. GIST**  
    *Correct: D. Patients with liver metastases from GIST had the best prognosis with 5-year and 10-year survival of 72% and 40%, respectively.*

4. **What is the median survival for patients with liver metastases from gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) after hepatic resection?**  
    A. 50 months  
    B. 75 months  
    C. 85 months  
    **D. 100 months**  
    *Correct: D. Patients with liver metastases from GIST had a median survival of 100 months after hepatic resection.*

5. **What is the 5-year survival rate for patients with liver metastases from biliary carcinoma after hepatic resection?**  
    A. 17%  
    B. 25%  
    C. 31%  
    **D. 17%**  
    *Correct: A. The 5-year survival rate for patients with liver metastases from biliary carcinoma was 17%.*

6. **Which factor was identified as an independent prognostic marker for survival in Andreou et al.'s study of NCNN liver metastases?**  
    A. Tumor size  
    B. Number of liver lesions  
    **C. Presence of more than one site of extrahepatic tumor disease**  
    D. Age of patient  
    *Correct: C. Andreou et al. identified only the presence of more than one site of extrahepatic tumor disease as an independent prognostic marker.*

7. **What was the 5-year overall survival rate in Andreou et al.'s cohort of 51 patients with NCNN liver metastases?**  
    A. 37%  
    B. 48%  
    C. 52%  
    **D. 58%**  
    *Correct: D. The 5-year overall survival rate was 58% in Andreou et al.'s study.*

8. **According to Fitzgerald et al.'s systematic review, which primary tumor site is associated with the longest expected survival after liver resection for NCNN metastases?**  
    A. Breast cancer  
    B. Gastrointestinal cancer  
    **C. Genitourinary primaries**  
    D. Melanoma  
    *Correct: C. Genitourinary primaries had the longest expected survival with a median of 63 months (range 5.4-142 months).*

9. **What is the median survival for patients with liver metastases from breast cancer after hepatic resection according to large studies?**  
    A. 35 months  
    B. 45 months  
    **C. 62 months**  
    D. 75 months  
    *Correct: C. Patients with liver metastases from breast cancer had a median survival of 62 months.*

10. **Which margin status is associated with the best cancer-specific survival after hepatectomy for NCNN metastases?**  
    A. R2  
    B. R1  
    **C. R0**  
    D. R0.1  
    *Correct: C. R0 resection (complete microscopic resection) is associated with the best cancer-specific survival.*

11. **What was the 30-day mortality rate in Weitz et al.'s series of 141 patients undergoing liver resection for NCNN metastases?**  
    **A. 0%**  
    B. 1.5%  
    C. 2%  
    D. 5%  
    *Correct: A. The 30-day mortality rate was 0% in Weitz et al.'s series.*

12. **According to Weitz et al., what was the 3-year cancer-specific survival rate after liver resection for NCNN metastases?**  
    A. 30%  
    **B. 57%**  
    C. 65%  
    D. 72%  
    *Correct: B. The 3-year cancer-specific survival rate was 57% (median 42 months).*

13. **Which primary tumor category had the best outcome after R0 resection according to Weitz et al.?**  
    A. Gastrointestinal tumors  
    B. Breast cancer  
    **C. Reproductive tract tumors**  
    D. Adrenocortical tumors  
    *Correct: C. Patients with a primary reproductive tract tumor who underwent R0 resection had the best outcome, with a 3-year cancer-specific survival of 78%.*

14. **What disease-free interval was used as a cutoff for prognostic stratification in Weitz et al.'s study?**  
    A. 12 months  
    **B. 24 months**  
    C. 36 months  
    D. 48 months  
    *Correct: B. A disease-free interval of 24 months was used as the cutoff for prognostic stratification.*

15. **For patients with non-reproductive tract primary tumors and a disease-free interval >24 months, what was the 3-year cancer-specific survival after R0 resection?**  
    A. 36%  
    **B. 72%**  
    C. 85%  
    D. 92%  
    *Correct: B. These patients had a 3-year cancer-specific survival of 72% and a 3-year relapse-free survival of 30%.*

16. **What was the 5-year overall survival rate for patients with liver metastases from sarcoma who underwent complete resection?**  
    A. 15%  
    B. 22%  
    **C. 30%**  
    D. 45%  
    *Correct: C. The 5-year overall survival rate was 30% with a median of 39 months for completely resected sarcoma liver metastases.*

17. **Which histologic types were most common among sarcoma liver metastases in DeMatteo et al.'s series?**  
    A. Liposarcoma and angiosarcoma  
    **B. GIST and leiomyosarcoma**  
    C. Rhabdomyosarcoma and synovial sarcoma  
    D. Fibrosarcoma and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor  
    *Correct: B. GISTs and leiomyosarcomas were the most common histologic findings in sarcoma liver metastases.*

18. **What disease-free interval was a significant adverse prognostic parameter for survival in sarcoma liver metastases?**  
    **A. Less than 24 months**  
    B. Less than 12 months  
    C. Less than 36 months  
    D. Less than 48 months  
    *Correct: A. A disease-free interval of less than 24 months was a significant adverse prognostic parameter for survival.*

19. **For patients with breast cancer liver metastases, what is the reported 5-year survival rate in more recent series?**  
    A. 25-35%  
    B. 35-45%  
    **C. 48-61%**  
    D. 65-75%  
    *Correct: C. 5-year survival was 48% to 61% in more recently published series for breast cancer liver metastases.*

20. **What percentage of patients with breast cancer have liver metastases as the only sign of disseminated disease?**  
    A. 1-3%  
    **B. 4-18%**  
    C. 20-25%  
    D. 30-35%  
    *Correct: B. Only in a minor subset (4%-18%) of patients with breast cancer are liver metastases the only sign of disseminated disease.*

21. **According to Mariani et al., what was the 3-year survival rate for patients with isolated liver metastases from breast cancer who underwent surgical intervention?**  
    A. 51%  
    **B. 80.7%**  
    C. 65.2%  
    D. 42.3%  
    *Correct: B. Mariani et al. reported a 3-year survival of 80.7% for patients with liver metastases and no additional extrahepatic disease who underwent surgical intervention.*

22. **What was the median survival for patients with liver metastases from breast cancer in Sadot et al.'s study?**  
    A. 32 months  
    B. 34 months  
    **C. 50 months**  
    D. 63 months  
    *Correct: C. Sadot et al. reported a median survival of 50 months for patients with breast cancer liver metastases.*

23. **Which factor was NOT identified as an adverse prognostic factor for survival after liver resection for breast cancer metastases in multiple studies?**  
    A. Node involvement of primary tumor  
    B. Multiple liver metastases  
    **C. Hormone receptor negative status**  
    D. Disease-free interval <12-24 months  
    *Correct: C. Hormone receptor positive status (estrogen/progesterone) is associated with increased survival, not negative status.*

24. **What percentage of patients with cutaneous melanoma develop liver metastases?**  
    A. 5-10%  
    **B. 15-20%**  
    C. 25-30%  
    D. 35-40%  
    *Correct: B. Cutaneous melanomas disseminate to the liver in 15% to 20% of patients with this metastatic disease.*

25. **What percentage of patients with liver metastases from uveal melanoma have the liver as the only organ of secondary disease?**  
    A. 10%  
    B. 25%  
    **C. 40%**  
    D. 60%  
    *Correct: C. In 40% of patients with liver metastases from uveal melanoma, the liver is the only organ of the secondary disease.*

26. **What was the median overall survival after hepatic surgery for uveal melanoma liver metastases in Mariani et al.'s study?**  
    A. 8 months  
    **B. 14 months**  
    C. 27 months  
    D. 38 months  
    *Correct: B. The median overall survival after hepatic surgery was 14 months compared with 8 months in those who had no surgery.*

27. **What was the median survival after R0 resection for uveal melanoma liver metastases in Mariani et al.'s study?**  
    A. 11 months  
    B. 17 months  
    **C. 27 months**  
    D. 38 months  
    *Correct: C. They observed a median overall survival of 27 months after R0 resection.*

28. **What was the 5-year survival rate for patients undergoing resection of uveal melanoma liver metastases in Hsueh et al.'s series?**  
    A. 19%  
    B. 25%  
    **C. 39%**  
    D. 52%  
    *Correct: C. The median survival for patients undergoing resection was 38 months, with a 5-year survival of 39%.*

29. **Compared to patients with cutaneous melanoma liver metastases, what was the 5-year survival for patients with ocular melanoma liver metastases?**  
    A. 0% for both  
    B. 0% for ocular, 21% for cutaneous  
    **C. 21% for ocular, 0% for cutaneous**  
    D. 21% for both  
    *Correct: C. The 5-year survival was significantly better for metastatic ocular melanoma (21% versus 0%; P=0.015).*

30. **What was the median time to recurrence after resection of ocular melanoma liver metastases in Pawlik et al.'s report?**  
    A. 5.2 months  
    **B. 8.8 months**  
    C. 12.4 months  
    D. 15.7 months  
    *Correct: B. The median time to recurrence was 8.8 months.*

31. **What percentage of patients with gastric cancer and liver-only metastases underwent hepatic resection with curative intent in Cheon et al.'s study?**  
    A. 45%  
    **B. 71%**  
    C. 85%  
    D. 92%  
    *Correct: B. Of 58 patients with liver-only metastases from gastric cancer, 41 (71%) underwent hepatic resection with curative intent.*

32. **What were the 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year survival rates for patients with gastric cancer who underwent curative hepatic resection?**  
    A. 85.2%, 41.5%, 28.7%  
    **B. 75.3%, 31.7%, 20.8%**  
    C. 68.9%, 25.4%, 15.2%  
    D. 57.6%, 18.3%, 9.5%  
    *Correct: B. The overall 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year survival rates were 75.3%, 31.7%, and 20.8%, respectively.*

33. **What was the median survival for patients undergoing combined pancreatic and liver resection for metastatic pancreatic cancer in Shrikhande et al.'s report?**  
    A. 5.8 months  
    B. 8.2 months  
    **C. 11.4 months**  
    D. 15.7 months  
    *Correct: C. The median survival was 11.4 months.*

34. **What is the estimated 5-year overall survival rate for patients with liver metastases from renal tumors who undergo metastasectomy?**  
    A. 29.3%  
    **B. 62.2%**  
    C. 45.7%  
    D. 39.0%  
    *Correct: B. The overall survival rate at 5 years after metastasectomy was 62.2%, with a median survival of 142 months.*

35. **How does the 5-year overall survival rate for renal cell carcinoma liver metastasectomy patients compare to controls who declined surgery?**  
    A. No difference  
    B. Slightly better (35.5% vs 29.3%)  
    **C. Significantly better (62.2% vs 29.3%)**  
    D. Worse (29.3% vs 62.2%)  
    *Correct: C. The 5-year overall survival rate was significantly higher in the surgical group (62.2% vs 29.3%, P=0.003).*

36. **What percentage of patients with liver metastases from renal tumors are candidates for complete resection?**  
    A. Less than 5%  
    **B. Approximately 2-4%**  
    C. About 10%  
    D. Nearly 15%  
    *Correct: B. Only approximately 2% to 4% experience hepatic disease that is amenable to complete resection.*

37. **What was the median survival for patients with ovarian carcinoma who underwent liver resection for metachronous metastases in Merideth et al.'s study?**  
    A. 18.2 months  
    **B. 26.3 months**  
    C. 35.7 months  
    D. 42.9 months  
    *Correct: B. Median disease-related survival was 26.3 months.*

38. **What factor was associated with improved outcome after liver resection for ovarian carcinoma metastases in Merideth et al.'s study?**  
    A. Younger age  
    B. Lower tumor grade  
    **C. Disease-free interval exceeding 12 months**  
    D. Hormone receptor positivity  
    *Correct: C. A disease-free interval exceeding 12 months and optimal cytoreduction were associated with improved outcome.*

39. **According to Lim et al., what was the 5-year overall survival rate for patients with stage IV ovarian cancer with hepatic parenchymal metastasis from peritoneal seeding?**  
    A. 23%  
    **B. 51%**  
    C. 37%  
    D. 18%  
    *Correct: B. The 5-year overall survival rate was 51% for patients with stage IV disease and hepatic parenchymal metastasis.*

40. **What was the median disease-free survival after complete resection of sarcoma liver metastases?**  
    A. 8 months  
    B. 12 months  
    **C. 12 months**

41. **What was the 5-year disease-specific survival for patients with sarcoma liver metastases who underwent complete resection compared to other treatments?**  
    **A. 30% vs 4%**

42. **What was the perioperative mortality rate in Triantafyllidis et al.'s evaluation of laparoscopic liver resections for NCNN metastases?**

43. **What were the 3-year and 5-year overall survival rates in Triantafyllidis et al.'s laparoscopic liver resection series for NCNN metastases?**

    **B. 71.4% and 52.9%**  
    C. 78.9% and 63.5%  
    D. 57.3% and 38.6%  
    *Correct: B. Overall survival rates at 3 and 5 years were 71.4% and 52.9%, respectively.*

44. **What percentage of patients with NCNN metastases underwent repeat laparoscopic liver resection for recurrent metastatic tumors in Triantafyllidis et al.'s series?**  
    A. 5.7%  
    B. 8.9%  
    **C. 14.3%**
